assertions.assert: It is long-lived: each request is `bot.ability.hearing.voice.identification.input` `{id, segments}` or, for direct identification, `{id, audio, sample_rate_hz, channels, start_seconds, end_seconds, output}`. Given `segments`, it clips nothing: the speech service's `identify` (one `POST {base}/voice/embed` per segment) answers `bot.ability.hearing.voice.identification.output` `{embeddings}`, and it answers its parent with `bot.ability.hearing.voice.identification.output` exactly `{id, segments, embeddings}`: the segments as given and one embedding per segment, in segment order, each `{embedding, model, confidence: null}`.
The `model` `<param>` names the embedding model (`voice-detect-wespeaker-resnet34` by default), and each embedding reports it.

Without `segments` it identifies directly: `clipping` invokes the speech service's `clip` on `audio` (`sample_rate_hz`, `channels`) over `start_seconds`..`end_seconds` (the end clamped to the sound) into `output`, and the one clipped segment `{audio: output, media_type: "audio/pcm", sample_rate_hz, channels, start_seconds, end_seconds}` is what it identifies and returns as `segments`.

When the clip answers `bot.ability.failed` `{message}` (a span that holds no audio, a sound that cannot be read), it answers `bot.ability.failed` `{id, message: "Voice identification opening segment conversion failed: <message>"}` and nothing is identified.
When the identification answers `bot.ability.failed` `{message}` (an error status, a malformed embedding), it answers `bot.ability.failed` exactly `{id, message}`.

When a step cannot run (segments that are not ascending `audio/pcm` voice segments, or no segments and no sound to clip, reject its start with `error.execution`), it answers `bot.ability.failed` `{id, message: "VoiceIdentification could not run (<error event>)"}`.
